prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge of engineering mathematics (fractions, polynomials, rational functions, partial fraction decomposition, differential and integral calculus, complex numbers) is mandatory.
Fundamental knowledge of electrical engineering and technical mechanics.
Ability to mathematically describe simple electrical and mechanical systems with elementary components (resistors, capacitors, inductors; masses, springs, dampers).
Ability to describe linear, time-invariant, continuous-time systems in the time and image domains, including familiarity with Laplace transforms.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will be taught the fundamentals for modeling and analysis of mechatronic systems.
Students will grasp the necessary theoretical/mathematical and practical fundamental knowledge for treating mechatronic systems.
Students will apply this knowledge (e.g., in exercises) to solve subject-specific problems.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical models for simple systems with mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic components (group work)
Description forms of (sub-)systems as two- and four-terminal networks
Introduction to the theory for describing digital signal processing

assessment_methods.method: Written exam or oral examination (Modulprüfung: Klausur oder mündliche Prüfung)

assessment_rules: The module examination consists of a written exam or an oral examination. The conduct and duration of the examination are according to the valid examination regulations. The module grade is based 100% on this assessment.
bibliography: An up-to-date literature list is included in the provided lecture materials.
